core_obligations: Reduce to the local question (proof lines 13066-13082): since internal hom commutes with restriction, it suffices to find a covering {U_i -> U} over whose members K^vee is perfect, and likewise for the two identifications; to see the final statement it is enough to check that the evaluation map M tensor^L K^vee -> RSheafHom(K, M) is an isomorphism, which is a local question as well.
Reduce to K strictly perfect (proof lines 13083-13085): by locality one may assume K is represented by a strictly perfect complex E^bullet.

Compute K^vee in that case (proof lines 13086-13133): the terms (E^n)^vee of the dual complex are computed by the strictly-perfectness lemma for internal hom, which gives that K^vee is represented by a strictly perfect complex and hence is perfect, and yields the functorial isomorphisms with RSheafHom(K, M) and with Hom in the derived category by taking H^0 over C.
proof_roadmap: Notice that internal hom and the evaluation map are local, so everything may be checked after restriction along a covering.
Assume K is represented by a strictly perfect complex E^bullet.
Identify K^vee with the dual complex of E^bullet using the strictly-perfect internal-hom lemma; perfection, the involution and the two functorial isomorphisms follow.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the derived dual K^vee = RSheafHom(K, O) of a perfect object K is perfect, that the double dual is K, and that K^vee represents both the internal hom and the Hom functor on the derived category (statement lines 13047-13063). The proof (proof lines 13065-13133) is a locality reduction: internal hom restricts, so perfection and the two identifications may be verified after passing to a covering, where K becomes a strictly perfect complex E^bullet, and the strictly-perfect internal-hom lemma computes the dual complex termwise. H2: two reductions followed by a termwise computation, all written out.
